subject: Question about calculating distances from lon/lat

messages.author: 8c8f0ca54c4a2459
messages.subject: Question about calculating distances from lon/lat
parts:
Hi all,

I am using spDists from the sp package to calculate the distance matrix for a set of points for which I have long/lat coordinates. The help file says:

spDists returns a full matrix of distances in the metric of the points if longlat=FALSE, or in kilometers if longlat=TRUE

Can someone explain to me what is meant by "the metric of the points"?

Thanks,

Noam

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Question about calculating distances from lon/lat
parts:
I think it should have been translated as "units", rather than "metric". The function returns Euclidean distance, the relevant part is pasted below, which will be in the units in which the points are specified.

        d = outer(x[, 1], y[, 1], "-")^2
        if (ncol(x) > 2) 
            for (i in 2:ncol(x)) d = d + outer(x[, i], y[, i], 
                "-")^2
        matrix(sqrt(d), nrow(x), nrow(y))

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Question about calculating distances from lon/lat
parts:
Basically it's just the units used in the coordinate reference system of
the spatial object under consideration. Often it's in meters, in some
cases it's in feet, but anything is possible.

-- Allan Hollander

messages.author: 8450e58469709b15
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Question about calculating distances from lon/lat
parts:
If you prefer a geographic explanation, when longlat=FALSE is set, the function treats the numbers as coordinates from a projection that is approximately equidistant within the area of interest, and calculates distances between them the way you would expect. The help file only mentions that it is preserving the "metric" because it cannot do this when longlat=TRUE is set (as is the case for your data) and the coordinates are not projected, and an arbitrary unit (km) has to be selected for the output.

GRB
